messages:
ryan: hey all -- first day! trying to build the runtime from source on Ubuntu 22.04, following BUILD.md. hitting a linker error during `make install` for the runtime plugin. any pointers?

ryan: full error snippet:```/usr/bin/ld: libs/libinfruntime.a(core.o): in function \`InitDevice\':
core.cpp:(.text+0x1a7f): undefined reference to \`cuInit\'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

emma: welcome! :wave: the undefined reference to cuInit usually means the linker isn't picking up libcuda/libcudart. did you set CUDA_HOME and add the right -L flags?

ryan: I set CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda-12.1 and `export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$CUDA_HOME/lib64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH` but still same. nvcc --version shows 12.1.

kai: double-check the toolchain. nvcc is picky about gcc versions. what's `gcc --version`?

ryan: `gcc (Ubuntu 11.4.0-1ubuntu1~22.04) 11.4.0`

maya: CUDA 12.x typically requires gcc <= 11, so that should be fine. but if you built libinfruntime.a with a different libstdc++ ABI or used a container with older glibc, linking can fail. did you build any deps with a different compiler?

ryan: I pulled prebuilt third_party libs from `third_party/prebuilt/linux-x86_64` (from the repo). Maybe those were built with GCC 9.

emma: aha. ABI mismatch is common. Two options: rebuild the third_party libs from source, or install a matching gcc and use update-alternatives to switch for the build. I usually repro with a dedicated docker dev image to avoid host mismatch.

ryan: if I switch gcc to 9 for the build, how do I keep system default at 11?

kai: use update-alternatives for just the build step or set CC/CXX env vars when running cmake. e.g.:
```bash
sudo update-alternatives --install /usr/bin/gcc gcc /usr/bin/gcc-9 90
sudo update-alternatives --install /usr/bin/g++ g++ /usr/bin/g++-9 90
# then configure your build, or set: CC=/usr/bin/gcc-9 CXX=/usr/bin/g++-9 cmake ..
```

maya: also check the link line in the failing target (re-run ninja with -v or `make VERBOSE=1`) to see if `-lcuda` or `-lcudart` is present.

ryan: thanks. re-ran with verbose and saw no `-lcudart` on the link line for the runtime binary. the cmake target is `inference_runtime`.

emma: probably missing `find_package(CUDART REQUIRED)` or the target_link_libraries line. In this repo we have a macro `add_cuda_runtime(libname)` in `cmake/modules/RedwoodCuda.cmake` — did that get included?

ryan: cmake output shows: "-- Found CUDA: /usr/local/cuda-12.1 (found version \"12.1\")" but I don't know about that macro.

kai: grep for `add_cuda_runtime` and `target_link_libraries(inference_runtime` to see how it's wired.

ryan: grep returns `add_cuda_runtime(inference_runtime)` in `src/runtime/CMakeLists.txt` and the macro definition is present. weird.

maya: could be a conditional macro that only adds libs if `ENABLE_CUDA` is ON. what's your cmake flags?

ryan: I ran `cmake -B build -S . -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo -DENABLE_CUDA=ON`

emma: hm. can you paste the verbose link line? also check if `CUDART_LIBRARY` variable is set in the cmake cache.

ryan: verbose link line (trimmed):```/usr/bin/c++  -O2 -g -Wl,--no-undefined -Wl,-z,relro -o bin/inference_runtime CMakeFiles/inference_runtime.dir/main.o libinfruntime.a -pthread -lrt -ldl```

ryan: looks like `-lcudart` missing indeed. CUDART_LIBRARY is not set in CMakeCache.txt

kai: try setting `-DCUDART_LIBRARY=$CUDA_HOME/lib64/libcudart.so` and reconfigure.

ryan: did `cmake -B build -S . -DENABLE_CUDA=ON -DCUDART_LIBRARY=/usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64/libcudart.so` then `cmake --build build -j8` — now link includes `-lcudart` but new error:```/usr/bin/ld: /usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64/libcudart_static.a(libcudart_static.a.o): relocation R_X86_64_32S against `.rodata' can not be used when making a shared object; recompile with -fPIC```

maya: that means you're pulling the static cudart instead of the shared one. make sure libcudart.so exists in lib64 and point CUDART_LIBRARY to the .so not the static archive. sometimes the symlinks are missing if toolkit was installed partially. `ls -l $CUDA_HOME/lib64/libcudart*`

ryan: `libcudart.so -> libcudart.so.12.1` and `libcudart_static.a` present too. I set the .so explicitly but still getting the static error.

emma: could be that CMake prefers the static archive because `CMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE` is OFF or because link order picks static first. Try forcing shared: `-DCUDART_LIBRARY=/usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64/libcudart.so -DCMAKE_SHARED_LINKER_FLAGS='-Wl,-Bdynamic'` or set `BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON` and `-DCMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE=ON`.

kai: another option: install `cuda-toolkit` from the distro's package manager or the runfile installer that guarantees the .so. If you're in WSL or custom kernel, sometimes the packaged .so is missing.

ryan: I turned on `-DCMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE=ON` and rebuilt, link succeeded! bin/inference_runtime runs and prints the warmup logs. :tada:

build-bot: [CI] ryan pushed branch feature/onboard-runtime-fix - started CI job #4821 (linux-cuda)

ryan: thanks everyone. last question: is there a recommended dev container for runtime work so I don't change my host gcc?

maya: yes, see `dev/containers/runtime-dev.Dockerfile` in repo. it has preinstalled gcc-9, cuda 12.1 userland and the right toolchain. we also have a `./scripts/dev_shell.sh` that launches it.

emma: if you want, ping me and I can pair for 15m to walk through the container and CI artifacts.

eng-runtime-oncall: if CI fails after your push, add `@eng-runtime-oncall` and we'll triage the build flakes.

ryan: will do. thanks again — feeling un-stuck now :relieved:
